world.title: North Korea fires two missiles as regional tensions rise
world.summary: North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea on Sunday, South Korea’s military said. The first launch took place around 3 p.m. local time and traveled roughly 450 kilometers. A second missile followed around 5:50 p.m. and flew more than 600 kilometers. Both weapons fell
world.content: North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area toward the East Sea on Sunday, South Korea’s military said. The first launch took place around 3 p.m. local time and traveled roughly 450 kilometers. A second missile followed around 5:50 p.m. and flew more than 600 kilometers. Both weapons fell into the sea, and Japan said they landed outside its exclusive economic zone. Pyongyang had rejected an International Atomic Energy Agency resolution concerning its nuclear activities and reaffirmed its nuclear-armed status. The launches also followed Pyongyang’s objections to U.S.-led military activity after President Trump’s decision last month to scale back a joint exercise with South Korea. South Korea convened an emergency security meeting, while South Korean, U.S. and Japanese authorities exchanged launch data.

world.title: Iran warns US of retaliation as Trump weighs strikes
world.summary: Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said Sunday that Tehran had information the United States was preparing to resume military action, with support from some regional countries. The command warned that any new US attack would trigger sustained strikes against American bases and interests across the Middle East
world.content: Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said Sunday that Tehran had information the United States was preparing to resume military action, with support from some regional countries. The command warned that any new US attack would trigger sustained strikes against American bases and interests across the Middle East and that countries supporting Washington could be treated as parties to the conflict. Iran has not provided details that independently verify the alleged preparations. President Donald Trump told Fox News he was in a “deciding mode” and said his options included further military action, economic pressure or a negotiated agreement. He said he would probably be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week. The US State Department separately urged Americans in Iran to leave and warned travelers of possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and border disruptions.
world.image_alt: Iran warns US of retaliation as Trump weighs strikes

world.title: Iran closes French language center; Paris to summon ambassador
world.summary: Iranian authorities sealed the French Language Centre (CLF), which is affiliated with France’s embassy in Tehran, on Sept. 20 on orders from the Tehran prosecutor’s office. Mizan, Iran’s judicial news website, reported allegations against the center, but the supplied reports did not independently substantiate them. Fra
world.content: Iranian authorities sealed the French Language Centre (CLF), which is affiliated with France’s embassy in Tehran, on Sept. 20 on orders from the Tehran prosecutor’s office. Mizan, Iran’s judicial news website, reported allegations against the center, but the supplied reports did not independently substantiate them. France said it would summon Iran’s ambassador in Paris and take appropriate measures. Paris has previously rejected Iranian allegations against the center, and French officials described the pressure as part of a broader pattern of intimidation as France seeks to maintain contact with Iranian civil society.
world.image_alt: Iran closes French language center; Paris to summon ambassador

world.title: Pakistan detains Imran Khan’s sisters before September 27 march
world.summary: Pakistani authorities detained Aleema Khan, a sister of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, in Lahore on September 20 and ordered her held for 30 days at Kot Lakhpat jail. The Lahore deputy commissioner’s order said she had mobilized Khan’s supporters through social media and public meetings and that her presence
world.content: Pakistani authorities detained Aleema Khan, a sister of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan, in Lahore on September 20 and ordered her held for 30 days at Kot Lakhpat jail. The Lahore deputy commissioner’s order said she had mobilized Khan’s supporters through social media and public meetings and that her presence in public could threaten public safety. Police confirmed the detention, while Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party called it illegal. Authorities detained two other sisters, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, on September 21 and transferred them to the same jail under 30-day Maintenance of Public Order orders, Pakistani media and family sources said. The detentions came ahead of a PTI-organized march toward Islamabad on September 27 seeking Imran Khan’s release and what the party calls constitutional supremacy. Officials have placed shipping containers around parts of Islamabad, while Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the government would take measures to stop the march.

world.title: Trump administration prepares sanctions against ICC as an institution
world.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration has prepared sanctions against the International Criminal Court itself and plans to announce them soon, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. The timing is unsettled, although U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal that a decision could be finali
world.content: President Donald Trump’s administration has prepared sanctions against the International Criminal Court itself and plans to announce them soon, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. The timing is unsettled, although U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal that a decision could be finalized during the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week or shortly afterward. The proposed measures would expand Washington’s existing sanctions on individual ICC judges and prosecutors. U.S. officials want the court to withdraw arrest warrants for Israeli leaders and end its previous investigation into American troops in Afghanistan; Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced a campaign in July to isolate the tribunal and urged countries to leave it. The United States and Israel are not members of the ICC and reject its jurisdiction in these cases.
world.image_alt: Trump administration prepares sanctions against ICC as an institution

world.title: Houthis attack Riyadh as Trump claims U.S. nonaggression deal
world.summary: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement fired missiles and drones toward Saudi Arabia over the weekend, including attacks on Riyadh and nearby airport facilities, as its forces advanced against Saudi-backed government forces inside Yemen. Saudi authorities said air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at the capi
world.content: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement fired missiles and drones toward Saudi Arabia over the weekend, including attacks on Riyadh and nearby airport facilities, as its forces advanced against Saudi-backed government forces inside Yemen. Saudi authorities said air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at the capital and other Houthi attacks, while reports described explosions and a fire near King Khalid International Airport. The strikes were the first Houthi missile attack on Riyadh since the Yemen conflict resumed. President Donald Trump said Washington was in constant communication with the Houthis and that they had agreed not to fight U.S. forces. Houthi political-bureau member Mohamed al-Bukhaiti separately told The Associated Press that the group would not target U.S. or other foreign vessels in the Red Sea, except Saudi vessels. He said contacts with Washington were indirect and mediated by Oman. The United States warned that the fighting could escalate rapidly, while the Houthis warned other countries against joining Saudi Arabia’s campaign.
world.image_alt: Houthis attack Riyadh as Trump claims U.S. nonaggression deal

world.title: Meloni proposes school veil ban, cap on foreign students
world.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Sunday, September 20, that her government would soon present a package to Italy’s Council of Ministers to ban burqas and niqabs in schools, set a legal maximum for foreign students in each class, and require parents of foreign students with serious integration difficulties to
world.content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Sunday, September 20, that her government would soon present a package to Italy’s Council of Ministers to ban burqas and niqabs in schools, set a legal maximum for foreign students in each class, and require parents of foreign students with serious integration difficulties to learn Italian. She announced the measures at Fenix, a Rome gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party, and did not specify the proposed student cap. Meloni said the measures would support integration and prevent Italian children from becoming a minority in their classrooms. Students without Italian citizenship account for 11.6% of Italy’s school population, or about 930,000 pupils, according to Fondazione ISMU. Italy already has a foreign-student limit in law, but the government has not explained how the proposed rule would differ. The package would require parliamentary approval after government adoption to become law.
world.image_alt: Meloni proposes school veil ban, cap on foreign students

world.title: Haiti sends 18 Moïse assassination suspects to Florida trial
world.summary: Haiti transferred 18 suspects in the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse to the United States on Sunday, Sept. 20, aboard a military aircraft. They will face federal proceedings in Florida over their alleged roles in the plot. U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones said 30 people have been indicted in the case.
world.content: Haiti transferred 18 suspects in the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse to the United States on Sunday, Sept. 20, aboard a military aircraft. They will face federal proceedings in Florida over their alleged roles in the plot. U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones said 30 people have been indicted in the case. Joseph Felix Badio, a former Haitian anti-corruption official identified by Haitian government and police sources as a central suspect, was among those transferred. Moïse, 53, was shot at his private residence in Port-au-Prince on July 7, 2021, by an armed group that included about 20 military-trained Colombian mercenaries. His security detail did not intervene, the reports said. The transfer followed five years without a trial in Haiti and came after four men were convicted in a Miami federal court in May 2026 in connection with the alleged plot.
world.image_alt: Haiti sends 18 Moïse assassination suspects to Florida trial

business.title: Fed official says inflation remains broad across US economy
business.summary: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari said U.S. inflation remains too high across the economy, even after excluding volatile energy and food prices. He said inflation had spread beyond the oil-price shock linked to intensified conflict in the Middle East and that the Federal Reserve’s task is to return in
business.content: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari said U.S. inflation remains too high across the economy, even after excluding volatile energy and food prices. He said inflation had spread beyond the oil-price shock linked to intensified conflict in the Middle East and that the Federal Reserve’s task is to return inflation to its 2% target. Kashkari backed the Federal Open Market Committee’s unanimous decision last week to raise its policy rate by a quarter percentage point, to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%. He was one of three officials who favored a rate increase at the prior meeting, when most policymakers left rates unchanged; projections released with the latest decision showed that all but two officials expected at least one more quarter-point increase this year.
business.image_alt: Fed official says inflation remains broad across US economy

business.title: US businesses face higher costs from tariffs, fuel and interest rates
business.summary: American companies face rising input, transport and financing costs as tariffs, higher fuel prices, interest rates, supply chain disruptions and weather-related shocks pressure manufacturers, auto suppliers, retailers and transportation businesses. Business owners interviewed in coverage described conditions as harder
business.content: American companies face rising input, transport and financing costs as tariffs, higher fuel prices, interest rates, supply chain disruptions and weather-related shocks pressure manufacturers, auto suppliers, retailers and transportation businesses. Business owners interviewed in coverage described conditions as harder to manage than during the Covid-19 supply-chain crisis, while customers resist further price increases. The Institute for Supply Management's monthly survey and accounts from company executives indicate that businesses are reducing inventories and finding medium-term planning more difficult.

business.title: France projects debt above 120% of GDP by 2027
business.summary: France’s public debt is projected to reach 119.3% of gross domestic product in 2026 and 121.7% in 2027, the highest levels since 1978, according to the finance ministry. The finance ministry attributed the increase to a deficit that remains high. France is the eurozone’s third-most indebted country after Greece and Ita
business.content: France’s public debt is projected to reach 119.3% of gross domestic product in 2026 and 121.7% in 2027, the highest levels since 1978, according to the finance ministry. The finance ministry attributed the increase to a deficit that remains high. France is the eurozone’s third-most indebted country after Greece and Italy. The government is preparing €54 billion in spending cuts for next year as it faces pressure to rein in its public finances.

business.title: US diesel prices top $6.50 as war strains fuel supplies
business.summary: U.S. retail diesel prices reached a record high, with the national average at $6.505 a gallon on Saturday, according to AAA. Bloomberg reported that prices topped $6.50 for the first time. The rise followed a 42-cent jump in one week and reflected disruptions linked to the war with Iran, tighter global refining capacit
business.content: U.S. retail diesel prices reached a record high, with the national average at $6.505 a gallon on Saturday, according to AAA. Bloomberg reported that prices topped $6.50 for the first time. The rise followed a 42-cent jump in one week and reflected disruptions linked to the war with Iran, tighter global refining capacity and pressure on fuel supplies. Diesel is used in trucking, rail, agriculture, construction, manufacturing, heating and the transport of consumer goods. Sustained high prices could increase freight, production and food costs. U.S. distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, have fallen to unusually low seasonal levels, while the approaching Northern Hemisphere heating season and disruptions affecting Middle Eastern and Russian fuel supplies are increasing competition for available products.
business.image_alt: US diesel prices top $6.50 as war strains fuel supplies

business.title: Trump announces AI Force before Xi visit
business.summary: President Trump announced plans to create a federal “AI Force” and appoint an artificial-intelligence adviser, often described as an AI czar, as Washington seeks to keep the United States ahead of China in advanced technology. He said his administration would not hinder the industry’s growth. The announcement preceded
business.content: President Trump announced plans to create a federal “AI Force” and appoint an artificial-intelligence adviser, often described as an AI czar, as Washington seeks to keep the United States ahead of China in advanced technology. He said his administration would not hinder the industry’s growth. The announcement preceded Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the United States this week, where artificial intelligence is expected to feature in discussions between the two leaders. The United States and China are competing for AI leadership while expressing concern about how AI in the other country’s hands could affect national security.
business.image_alt: Trump announces AI Force before Xi visit

business.title: Older laid-off workers face jobs and insurance gaps
business.summary: Peter Wade writes in the Guardian that he is in his 61st year, has been out of work for more than two years and has stopped applying for jobs. He argues that employment policy should address people who lose work near state pension age as well as unemployed young people. In the United States, older laid-off workers who
business.content: Peter Wade writes in the Guardian that he is in his 61st year, has been out of work for more than two years and has stopped applying for jobs. He argues that employment policy should address people who lose work near state pension age as well as unemployed young people. In the United States, older laid-off workers who have not yet reached Medicare eligibility can have difficulty obtaining health insurance before age 65. The Guardian letter also describes the difficulty of continuing physically demanding work after changes to the women’s state pension age extended the time before some women qualified for the state pension.
business.image_alt: Older laid-off workers face jobs and insurance gaps

business.title: Canada and France deepen ties as EU alliance advances
business.summary: Canada and France agreed to expand cooperation in energy, defense, space, telecommunications, climate resilience and business after Prime Minister Mark Carney met President Emmanuel Macron on Sept. 20 in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, a French territory off Newfoundland. The meeting followed a European Commission proposal f
business.content: Canada and France agreed to expand cooperation in energy, defense, space, telecommunications, climate resilience and business after Prime Minister Mark Carney met President Emmanuel Macron on Sept. 20 in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, a French territory off Newfoundland. The meeting followed a European Commission proposal for Canada to become the European Union’s first associate member, as Ottawa seeks alternatives after worsening trade relations with the United States. Macron endorsed closer Canadian ties with the EU, while Carney said Canada and Europe should build an alliance that reduces vulnerability to economic pressure from any one country. Canada and France instructed their space agencies and defense ministries to develop shared launch and satellite-data reception infrastructure. Macron said Canadian liquefied natural gas projects could create new opportunities for Europe, while Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne urged the United Kingdom to join a proposed Canada-Europe economic alliance.
business.image_alt: Canada and France deepen ties as EU alliance advances

business.title: Tata family feud escalates toward legal showdown
business.summary: Noel Tata, a senior member of India’s Tata family, is preparing to challenge the reappointment of Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, according to an Indian report. The dispute between Tata Sons and Tata Trusts could lead to a courtroom battle over control and governance. The conflict also concerns whether Tata Sons,
business.content: Noel Tata, a senior member of India’s Tata family, is preparing to challenge the reappointment of Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, according to an Indian report. The dispute between Tata Sons and Tata Trusts could lead to a courtroom battle over control and governance. The conflict also concerns whether Tata Sons, the group’s holding company, should be listed. The Financial Times reported that Noel Tata is seeking to avert a listing. Rival camps are preparing for a legal battle that could reach Indian courts and Narendra Modi’s government, Business Times reported.
business.image_alt: Tata family feud escalates toward legal showdown

science.title: Oregon Coast astronomy guide highlights comets and nebulae
science.summary: A collection of astronomy articles from the Oregon and Washington coasts highlights objects and phenomena that are difficult or impossible to see without optical equipment. It features Comet 12P/Pons-Brooks, which erupted after solar radiation heated material inside its icy interior, and astrophotographs taken at Otter
science.content: A collection of astronomy articles from the Oregon and Washington coasts highlights objects and phenomena that are difficult or impossible to see without optical equipment. It features Comet 12P/Pons-Brooks, which erupted after solar radiation heated material inside its icy interior, and astrophotographs taken at Otter Rock near Newport, Oregon, on March 31, 2024. The collection explains that emission nebulae can appear as pink or red structures in long-exposure photographs even though they are not visible to the naked eye. Other articles discuss a satellite photographed above Cape Kiwanda in an exposure of about 10 seconds and night photography near Astoria, where clear coastal skies and specialized cameras can reveal details not visible under ordinary viewing conditions.
science.image_alt: Oregon Coast astronomy guide highlights comets and nebulae

science.title: NASA
science.summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope activated its 300-megapixel camera and produced its first test image, showing hundreds of stars as green rings of light. NASA shared the image on Sept. 15 as the telescope continues a months-long tuning period. After several more months of adjustments, NASA expects Roman to capt
science.content: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope activated its 300-megapixel camera and produced its first test image, showing hundreds of stars as green rings of light. NASA shared the image on Sept. 15 as the telescope continues a months-long tuning period. After several more months of adjustments, NASA expects Roman to capture Hubble-like sharp images across a field 100 times larger, according to Live Science.

science.title: UC Riverside study suggests Venus swallowed an ancient moon
science.summary: A University of California, Riverside study suggests Venus may once have had a moon that spiraled inward and collided with the planet, potentially explaining why Venus has no natural satellite today. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal.
science.content: A University of California, Riverside study suggests Venus may once have had a moon that spiraled inward and collided with the planet, potentially explaining why Venus has no natural satellite today. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal.

science.title: Satellite record shows polar ice loss accelerated since 1979
science.summary: An international assessment of satellite observations found that Greenland and Antarctica lost about 11.3 trillion metric tons of ice between 1979 and 2023, equivalent to 12.5 trillion U.S. tons. The loss raised global sea levels by about 3.1 centimeters. If spread evenly, the lost ice would cover the continental Unite
science.content: An international assessment of satellite observations found that Greenland and Antarctica lost about 11.3 trillion metric tons of ice between 1979 and 2023, equivalent to 12.5 trillion U.S. tons. The loss raised global sea levels by about 3.1 centimeters. If spread evenly, the lost ice would cover the continental United States with roughly 1.5 meters of water. The assessment found that about 84% of the combined decline resulted from ice-dynamic changes, including faster glacier movement toward the ocean and increased ice discharge, rather than surface melting or changes in snowfall alone. Greenland’s annual loss rose from about 60 billion metric tons in the 1980s to an average of 264 billion metric tons in the 2010s, while Antarctic losses reached about 202 billion metric tons annually during the 2010s.
science.image_alt: Satellite record shows polar ice loss accelerated since 1979

science.title: T. rex teeth reveal human-like body temperature, study finds
science.summary: Researchers have made the first direct estimate of Tyrannosaurus rex body temperature from fossilized teeth, finding an average of about 36.3°C, or roughly 97°F—close to the human average of 37°C and the modern elephant’s approximately 36°C. The team, led by UCLA geochemists Randon J. Flores and Robert A. Eagle, analyz
science.content: Researchers have made the first direct estimate of Tyrannosaurus rex body temperature from fossilized teeth, finding an average of about 36.3°C, or roughly 97°F—close to the human average of 37°C and the modern elephant’s approximately 36°C. The team, led by UCLA geochemists Randon J. Flores and Robert A. Eagle, analyzed chemical signatures preserved in T. rex tooth enamel using a method designed to estimate temperatures in ancient animals. The estimate is consistent with evidence that T. rex generated and regulated substantial internal heat. T. rex fossils have been found as far north as Alaska. The estimate has an uncertainty of plus or minus 2.5°C, and the study examined three teeth discovered in Montana.
science.image_alt: T. rex teeth reveal human-like body temperature, study finds

science.title: Study links internet expansion to declining religious identity
science.summary: A cross-national study published in *Sociology of Religion: A Quarterly Review* links expanding internet access within countries to declines in religious affiliation and self-identification. Researchers examined whether digital connectivity may contribute to secularization alongside established modernization factors, i
science.content: A cross-national study published in *Sociology of Religion: A Quarterly Review* links expanding internet access within countries to declines in religious affiliation and self-identification. Researchers examined whether digital connectivity may contribute to secularization alongside established modernization factors, including rising wealth, education and urbanization.
science.image_alt: Study links internet expansion to declining religious identity

science.title: REM sleep linked to lower risk across 83 diseases
science.summary: A study of 95,559 participants in a UK health project found that people who spent more time in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep had lower observed risks of 83 diseases. Researchers led by Capital Medical University in China used wrist-worn trackers to measure sleep patterns for one week and compared them with more than 1
science.content: A study of 95,559 participants in a UK health project found that people who spent more time in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep had lower observed risks of 83 diseases. Researchers led by Capital Medical University in China used wrist-worn trackers to measure sleep patterns for one week and compared them with more than 1,000 health conditions over a median follow-up of nearly nine years. The study identified associations and did not show that changing REM sleep prevents disease.
science.image_alt: REM sleep linked to lower risk across 83 diseases

science.title: Brain scans find menopause temporarily slows cortical aging
science.summary: A study of more than 1,000 people suggests that menopause temporarily alters the brain’s pattern of age-related remodeling. Repeated scans found that the gradual loss of cortical volume and gray matter appeared to slow at the start of the menopausal transition, unlike the accelerated volume reductions observed during p
science.content: A study of more than 1,000 people suggests that menopause temporarily alters the brain’s pattern of age-related remodeling. Repeated scans found that the gradual loss of cortical volume and gray matter appeared to slow at the start of the menopausal transition, unlike the accelerated volume reductions observed during puberty and pregnancy. Researchers examined participants at different life stages, including before and after pregnancy and menopause, and found distinct structural changes in each phase. The study’s authors said it remains unclear why the menopause-related pattern occurs; the findings describe changes in brain structure, not whether menopause improves or worsens cognition.
science.image_alt: Brain scans find menopause temporarily slows cortical aging

sports.title: Australia complete Zimbabwe ODI sweep in one-wicket thriller
sports.summary: Australia beat Zimbabwe by one wicket in the third ODI at Harare Sports Club on Sunday to complete a 3-0 series sweep. Zimbabwe posted 271-8 after captain Sikandar Raza made an unbeaten 81, while Craig Ervine scored 59 and Innocent Kaia made 55 before retiring hurt. Australia reached 272-9 with one ball remaining after
sports.content: Australia beat Zimbabwe by one wicket in the third ODI at Harare Sports Club on Sunday to complete a 3-0 series sweep. Zimbabwe posted 271-8 after captain Sikandar Raza made an unbeaten 81, while Craig Ervine scored 59 and Innocent Kaia made 55 before retiring hurt. Australia reached 272-9 with one ball remaining after losing wickets regularly during the chase. Josh Inglis anchored Australia’s pursuit with 103, his second ODI century, before Nathan Ellis finished unbeaten on 36 from 44 balls. Australia needed 27 runs when Ellis was joined by No. 11 Spencer Johnson; Ellis hit a six from the first ball of the final over and struck the winning runs from the penultimate delivery. Australia travel to South Africa for three ODIs beginning in Durban on Thursday.
sports.image_alt: Australia complete Zimbabwe ODI sweep in one-wicket thriller

sports.title: JJ Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship after Presidents Cup snub
sports.summary: JJ Spaun won the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth on Sunday, September 20, shooting a final-round 67 to finish 17 under par, two shots ahead of Rory McIlroy, Manuel Elvira, Aaron Rai and Adam Scott. The victory came in Spaun’s first appearance in the DP World Tour’s flagship event, after he made four birdies over his
sports.content: JJ Spaun won the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth on Sunday, September 20, shooting a final-round 67 to finish 17 under par, two shots ahead of Rory McIlroy, Manuel Elvira, Aaron Rai and Adam Scott. The victory came in Spaun’s first appearance in the DP World Tour’s flagship event, after he made four birdies over his final five holes. McIlroy finished tied for second at 15 under after a late challenge but missed several birdie chances, including a putt on the 18th that would have kept him in contention. The result moved him within 307.76 points of Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed. Elvira lost the lead after making an eagle at the 17th, then a double bogey on the final hole.
sports.image_alt: JJ Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship after Presidents Cup snub

sports.title: Liverpool beat Bournemouth as Isak seals Iraola
sports.summary: Liverpool defeated Bournemouth 1-0 at the Vitality Stadium on September 20, with Alexander Isak scoring the decisive goal in the 57th minute after Cody Gakpo’s attacking work created the opening. The victory gave manager Andoni Iraola a winning return to the club he left for Liverpool, while Bournemouth remained withou
sports.content: Liverpool defeated Bournemouth 1-0 at the Vitality Stadium on September 20, with Alexander Isak scoring the decisive goal in the 57th minute after Cody Gakpo’s attacking work created the opening. The victory gave manager Andoni Iraola a winning return to the club he left for Liverpool, while Bournemouth remained without a Premier League victory under successor Marco Rose. Liverpool lacked attacking fluency but protected their lead effectively. Goalkeeper Alisson denied Evanilson in the first half, and Liverpool recorded a third consecutive Premier League clean sheet. Liverpool remained unbeaten in the league and entered the international break sixth, while Bournemouth sat 17th with three points.
sports.image_alt: Liverpool beat Bournemouth as Isak seals Iraola

sports.title: Chinese 13-year-old Yu Zidi sets Asian Games record
sports.summary: China’s 13-year-old Yu Zidi won the women’s 200m butterfly at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Tokyo on September 20 to claim her first major individual international title in 2:05.08. Her time cut nearly half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei’s 2:05.57 Games record, set at Hangzhou in 2023. Yu finished 3.36 seconds a
sports.content: China’s 13-year-old Yu Zidi won the women’s 200m butterfly at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Tokyo on September 20 to claim her first major individual international title in 2:05.08. Her time cut nearly half a second off compatriot Zhang Yufei’s 2:05.57 Games record, set at Hangzhou in 2023. Yu finished 3.36 seconds ahead of silver medallist Chang Mohan. Yu said she could swim faster and cited lowering her head earlier and improving her leg movement as areas to refine. China won six of seven finals in the opening swimming session. Yu is scheduled to race two more individual events at the Games.
sports.image_alt: Chinese 13-year-old Yu Zidi sets Asian Games record

sports.title: Bears lose 9-3 to Vikings after Caleb Williams exits with injury
sports.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams left Sunday’s 9-3 home loss to the Minnesota Vikings after suffering a right hamstring injury on a non-contact fourth-quarter scramble in Minnesota territory. Chicago ruled him out for the remainder of the game, and coach Ben Johnson said the team expected more information after
sports.content: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams left Sunday’s 9-3 home loss to the Minnesota Vikings after suffering a right hamstring injury on a non-contact fourth-quarter scramble in Minnesota territory. Chicago ruled him out for the remainder of the game, and coach Ben Johnson said the team expected more information after further evaluation on Monday. The Vikings improved to 2-0 after holding Chicago to 297 yards and three points. Aaron Jones Sr. rushed for 105 yards, and Dallas Turner recorded two of Minnesota’s four sacks. Tyson Bagent replaced Williams, but Isaiah Rodgers blocked Chicago’s potential game-tying 23-yard field-goal attempt. Williams finished 15-for-26 for 138 yards, an interception and 42 rushing yards on five carries.
sports.image_alt: Bears lose 9-3 to Vikings after Caleb Williams exits with injury

sports.title: Chiefs edge Colts 33-30 in overtime thriller
sports.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in overtime at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, September 20, improving to 2-0 and extending their overtime winning streak to six games. Patrick Mahomes completed 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns, connecting with Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy and
sports.content: The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Indianapolis Colts 33-30 in overtime at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, September 20, improving to 2-0 and extending their overtime winning streak to six games. Patrick Mahomes completed 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns, connecting with Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy and Jalen Royals. Harrison Butker kicked two overtime field goals, including a 40-yarder as time expired, after the teams finished regulation tied 27-27. Kenneth Walker III rushed for 117 yards and added 61 receiving yards, while Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards and a touchdown. Kansas City initially appeared to recover a fumble after Laquon Treadwell's 48-yard overtime catch, but replay ruled Treadwell down by contact. The Colts then tied the game before Kansas City mounted the decisive drive.
sports.image_alt: Chiefs edge Colts 33-30 in overtime thriller

sports.title: Leeds stay unbeaten after goalless draw with Palace
sports.summary: Leeds United remained unbeaten after drawing 0-0 with Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Sunday, September 20. sports.content: Leeds United remained unbeaten after drawing 0-0 with Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Sunday, September 20. The result left Leeds fifth with nine points from five Premier League matches, while Palace moved one point clear of the relegation zone after a much-improved defensive display. sports.content: Great Britain defeated Ecuador 3-0 in London to qualify for the Davis Cup Final 8, with Henry Patten and Neal Skupski sealing the tie with a 6-3, 6-4 doubles victory over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo on September 20. Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery won the opening singles matches on Saturday, giving Britain an unassailable lead before the doubles rubber. The result sends Leon Smith’s team to Bologna for the knockout stage, to be held from November 24 to 29. Britain will join defending champion Italy, Germany, Canada, Czechia, South Korea, Austria and Spain. Britain reached the quarter-final stage for the first time since 2023 despite late withdrawals and injuries affecting the squad, including Cameron Norrie’s arm problem and the unavailability of Jack Draper, Jan Choinski and Jacob Fearnley.
